sentences.l2: 三十岁以后，许多上班族开始重新审视自己的职业道路。
sentences.l1: After the age of thirty, many office workers begin to re-examine their career paths.

sentences.l2: 白天在办公室重复着熟悉却缺乏热情的工作，夜晚则打开电脑，听一堂关于数据分析的网课。
sentences.l1: During the day they repeat work that is familiar but lacking in passion at the office, and at night they open the computer and listen to an online class on data analysis.

sentences.l2: 这种在业余时间给自己充电的方式，看似辛苦，却为一次彻底的转行积蓄着力量。
sentences.l1: This way of recharging oneself in spare time seems hard, but it is building up strength for a complete career change.

sentences.l2: 与传统夜校相比，网课打破了时间与空间的限制：学习者可以在通勤的地铁上复习笔记，也可以在周末反复回看难懂的部分。
sentences.l1: Compared with traditional night school, online classes break the limits of time and space: learners can review notes on the subway during the commute, and can also rewatch the difficult parts again and again on weekends.

sentences.l2: 完成课程后，他们通常还要考取一份行业认可的证书，因为证书不仅是能力的证明，也是让新雇主愿意给出机会的通行证。
sentences.l1: After completing the course, they usually still have to obtain a certificate recognized by the industry, because a certificate is not only proof of ability but also a pass that makes a new employer willing to give an opportunity.

sentences.l2: 转行从来不是一时冲动的决定，它意味着接受暂时的收入下降与周围人的质疑。
sentences.l1: A career change is never an impulsive decision; it means accepting a temporary drop in income and the doubts of the people around them.

sentences.l2: 然而，正是这些愿意终身学习的人，逐渐把职业的主动权握在自己手中。
sentences.l1: However, it is precisely these people willing to learn for life who gradually take the initiative in their careers into their own hands.

sentences.l2: 对他们而言，学习不再是为了考试，而是一种生活方式。
sentences.l1: For them, learning is no longer for exams, but a way of life.
